faq.q: What is the origin of Katayoun?
faq.a: Katayoun is associated with Persian. Katayoun is Persian کتایون (Katāyūn), the name of a legendary queen in the Shahnameh. It is used as a female given name in Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Katayoun can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Katayoun should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Katāyūn is a Persian name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Katayoun mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Katayoun is rendered کتایون and carries the sense کتایون، فارسی ملکہ.

faq.q: What does Katayoun mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Katayoun is rendered کتایون and carries the sense کتایون، ملکه افسانه‌ای.
A romanized syllable approximation is ka-tayoun. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Katayoun?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Katayoun, katayoun. Script forms are كَتَايُون, کتايون, کتایون, कतायून.

faq.q: Is Katayoun a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
